q: In our 6 IncFIB-positive Typhimurium assemblies, the plasmid-encoded sitA-D + iucA-C operon and the IncFIB(AP001918) rep gene consistently land on DIFFERENT assembly contigs (~15–20 kb sit/iuc contig vs a separate rep contig), even though both should be on the same ~140 kb replicon. Is this a repeat-mediated assembly break at a specific location (e.g. IS200/IS26 or a tra/traD element) that is systematically present in these Illumina-only assemblies, or is it a genuine biological plasmid architecture (e.g. co-integrate with a smaller replicon)?
basis: All 6 Typhimurium strains in this replication showed the same pattern of sit+iuc on one contig, IncFIB rep on another (evidence/plasmid/incfib_hits.tsv + evidence/iron/iron_operon_hits_v3.tsv). This was not addressed in the paper because they used complete/hybrid assemblies where the whole plasmid was contiguous.
next_steps: Long-read (Oxford Nanopore R10.4 or PacBio Sequel II HiFi) resequencing of any ONE of the 6 strains (SE163A is the most-cited), assemble with Unicycler hybrid mode + Flye + circularise with Circlator, then verify the entire ~140 kb IncFIB plasmid is a single closed circular replicon with the rep gene and sit+iuc operon in cis. Then align back the Illumina contigs to identify the exact repeat-mediated break point.

q: SE397 is the outlier in our mash-based phylogeny (mean intra-group d = 4.3×10⁻³, vs 1.4–1.8×10⁻³ for the other 5), matching the paper's 5+1 topology. But mash cannot resolve whether SE397 is genuinely sister to bovine-source Typhimurium — the paper claims it does. What core-SNP-alignment-scale evidence supports (or refutes) a bovine origin for this specifically turkey-diagnostic-2002 isolate, and does SE397 carry bovine-Typhimurium-associated accessory genes (e.g. Fels-1, ST313 pseudogenes) that the other 5 lack?
basis: Our NJ tree from mash distances put SE397 near LT2/bovine cluster but did not resolve sister-group status; the paper's core-SNP tree (Fig 1b) resolved it clearly.
next_steps: Run Parsnp against LT2 reference on all 7 focal + ~10 bovine Typhimurium comparators (paper's Table 1 lists them) → RAxML on core-SNP alignment → identify SE397's sister lineage with bootstrap support. Separately, run panaroo pangenome analysis to identify accessory-gene bins over-represented in SE397 vs the other 5 turkey Typhimurium.

q: Both SE819 (Heidelberg, IncFIB-deficient recipient) and the 6 IncFIB(+) Typhimurium strains carry a chromosomal sit locus. Our tblastn shows the SE819 chromosomal sitA-D at 68–86% AA identity to the plasmid sitA-D reference (from pCVM29188_146). Is this differential — plasmid sit at 100% conserved across 6 Typhimurium vs chromosomal sit at 68–86% divergent from plasmid sit — driven by ongoing plasmid-borne purifying selection (implying active plasmid transmission maintains sequence identity), or by recent HGT of the plasmid sit locus from a distant Enterobacteriaceae donor into the Typhimurium plasmid pool?
basis: The 99.65–100% AA identity of plasmid-borne sitA-D + iucA-C across 6 independently isolated strains (3+ US states, 1992–2002) is striking evidence of very recent common ancestry OR ongoing purifying selection; the paper reports this conservation but does not interrogate its origin.
next_steps: Compute dN/dS across the plasmid sitABCD alignment vs the chromosomal sitABCD alignment using PAML codeml (M0 vs M1a vs M2a models); ω<<1 on plasmid but ω closer to neutral on chromosome would support ongoing purifying selection on the plasmid copy. Also BLAST the plasmid sit against non-Enterobacteriaceae to identify the source lineage.

q: The paper's Caco-2 persistence assay (SE819::IncFIB > SE819 recipient) attributes the phenotype to the whole IncFIB plasmid, but the plasmid also carries pef (fimbriae) and virulence-associated ORFs beyond sit+iuc. Can we in silico dissect which plasmid-encoded factor(s) — sit/iuc iron acquisition, pef adhesion, spv, or something else — carry the causal signal for Caco-2 persistence, using published RNA-seq/ChIP-seq data from Salmonella intracellular models?
basis: This replication confirmed sit+iuc are present on the plasmid but the plasmid also carries additional virulence loci that the paper did not assay individually. The pef and spv loci are separately known Caco-2/gut-persistence factors.
next_steps: Cross-reference against SalCom (Salmonella intracellular transcriptome database) and Kroger et al. 2013 macrophage RNA-seq to check which of {sitA-D, iucA-D, iutA, pefA-D, spvA-D, mig-14, virK, pgtE} are UP-regulated in Caco-2 or J774 intracellular niches. Then in a follow-up wet-lab study, plasmid-deletion constructs (Δsit, Δiuc, Δpef individually and combinatorially) would resolve the causal factor.

q: PlasmidFinder detected multiple additional Inc/Col replicons in the 6 Typhimurium isolates (IncFIA, IncFII variants, IncA, IncX4, IncI1, IncC, ColRNAI, ColpVC) at 83–100% identity — but the paper focused exclusively on IncFIB. Are any of these additional replicons present as CO-integrates with the IncFIB (i.e. the same physical plasmid carries multiple rep genes and is a hybrid ~200+ kb replicon), or as separate small plasmids? If co-integrates exist, they may be co-transferred during conjugation and confound attribution of Caco-2 phenotype to IncFIB specifically.
basis: Our plasmid/plasmidfinder_hits.tsv shows a rich multi-replicon Inc profile per strain not addressed in the paper's narrative.
next_steps: Take one long-read closed assembly (see Q1 next_steps) and map all Inc rep genes onto the closed plasmids to determine whether each rep is on a separate replicon or several are co-located on a single co-integrate. Then re-do the SE819::IncFIB transconjugant analysis on the *closed* transconjugant plasmid to confirm it carries ONLY IncFIB and not accidental co-transferred replicons.
